GenOffice
Copyright 2026 Mainfunc, Inc.

This product includes software developed at Mainfunc, Inc.

Bundled third-party components are listed in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, which
tools/gen-third-party-notices.mjs generates at packaging time. It is not
checked into this repository; in a release build it ships inside the
application bundle (Contents/Resources on macOS, resources/ on Windows),
starting with the full text of this file, next to LICENSE.txt (the Apache
License 2.0), NOTICE.txt (this file) and LICENSE-UNICODE.txt. Run
`node tools/gen-third-party-notices.mjs` to produce it from a source
checkout.

Bundled fonts and their licenses are documented in
apps/docs/src/renderer/fonts/README.md. The slide design templates' fonts
are listed under "Slide design template fonts" below.

Unicode Character Database

apps/pdf/src/shared/radicals.ts contains a generated mapping derived from
Unicode Character Database 17.0.0, EquivalentUnifiedIdeograph.txt
(2025-08-01):
https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/EquivalentUnifiedIdeograph.txt

Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc. This data is distributed under Unicode
License v3. The complete copyright and permission notice is reproduced in
LICENSE-UNICODE.txt.

Office Open XML schemas

tools/ooxml-validate/schemas contains the ISO/IEC 29500-4:2016 (ECMA-376
Part 4, Transitional) XML Schema files for PresentationML and DrawingML, as
distributed in the python-docx repository (ref/xsd), with one marked local
amendment (see tools/ooxml-validate/README.md). They are used only by tests
and development tooling and are not shipped in the application.

IeumOffice brand artwork

The IeumOffice app icon, logo lockup and AI button mark are original
compositions for this project: the sources in apps/shell/build/brand, the icon
and logo files tools/gen-brand-assets.mjs derives from them, and
packages/ui/src/AiMark.tsx. Their geometry is adapted from the Lucide icon set
(https://lucide.dev), icons `circle`, `square`, `link` and `message-square`.

Lucide is distributed under the ISC License, Copyright (c) Lucide Icons and
Contributors. The `circle`, `square` and `link` icons are derived from the
Feather project and are distributed under the MIT License, Copyright (c)
2013-present Cole Bemis. Both licenses permit use, modification and
redistribution provided their copyright and permission notices are kept; the
full texts are at https://github.com/lucide-icons/lucide/blob/main/LICENSE.

The wordmark in the logo lockup is set in Roboto Bold 2.137, Copyright 2011
Google Inc., licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, and converted to
outlines.

Slide design templates

The twelve built-in slide design templates in
packages/pipelines/src/slides/templates (coral, blue-professional,
monochrome, neo-grid-bold, block-frame, raw-grid, studio, signal, grove,
editorial-tri-tone, emerald-editorial, vellum) are re-authored from the
designs in frontend-slides (https://github.com/zarazhangrui/frontend-slides),
folder bold-template-pack/, read at commit
9906a34d640d2111f724544cbc50f7f130569ae1. The templates' style texts and
sample covers are based on those designs. frontend-slides is distributed

Slide design template fonts

packages/ui/template-fonts holds the fonts the design templates use. It
ships once in the installer as resources/template-fonts. Every file is the
original distributor's, unmodified, except the two Noto Serif KR faces, whose
CFF outlines are converted to TrueType (names and metrics unchanged); all are
licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1. Each family's license text sits beside its files, and
packages/ui/template-fonts/README.md records the license evidence and the
exact source of every file. All files were downloaded on 2026-10-14.

- Pretendard 1.309 (release v1.3.9), SIL OFL 1.1 with Reserved Font Name
  "Pretendard", https://github.com/orioncactus/pretendard
- Noto Serif KR 2.003, SIL OFL 1.1 (Reserved Font Name "Source"), outlines
  converted to TrueType, https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk
- Black Han Sans 1.001, SIL OFL 1.1,
  https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/blackhansans
- Do Hyeon 1.001, SIL OFL 1.1,
  https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/dohyeon
- Gowun Dodum 2.000, SIL OFL 1.1,
  https://github.com/yangheeryu/Gowun-Dodum
- Gowun Batang 2.000, SIL OFL 1.1,
  https://github.com/yangheeryu/Gowun-Batang
- Bebas Neue 2.000, SIL OFL 1.1,
  https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/bebasneue
- Space Grotesk 2.000, SIL OFL 1.1,
  https://github.com/floriankarsten/space-grotesk
- Playfair Display 1.203, SIL OFL 1.1 with Reserved Font Name
  "Playfair Display", https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/playfairdisplay
- Archivo Black 1.006, SIL OFL 1.1,
  https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/archivoblack

Built-in skills

apps/shell/resources/builtin-skills holds the five skills shipped with the
app. It ships in the installer as resources/builtin-skills. Each folder is the
upstream skill as read at the commit below, with its license file beside it;
builtin-skills.json in the same folder records the same source, path, commit
and license. Only the files listed for each skill were taken.

- meeting-minutes: https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot, path
  skills/meeting-minutes (SKILL.md), read at commit
  613efc8c21d9b3ce642dff361d17006cd9967e28. MIT License, Copyright GitHub,
  Inc.; the repository's LICENSE is copied as meeting-minutes/LICENSE.
  Unmodified.
- internal-comms: https://github.com/anthropics/skills, path
  skills/internal-comms (SKILL.md, LICENSE.txt, examples/), read at commit
  dbd4588f9e1033efb41dad4bef2f7947c8993d44. Apache License, Version 2.0,
  Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC; the full text is internal-comms/LICENSE.txt.
  Unmodified.
- humanizer: https://github.com/blader/humanizer, repository root (SKILL.md,
  LICENSE), read at commit 8c307f367c91bd974002f10f2be2965d642c13df. MIT
  License, Copyright (c) 2025 Siqi Chen. Unmodified.
- copy-editing: https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills, path
  skills/copy-editing (SKILL.md, references/), read at commit
  e85f3cbc2e4a79bf33b2a12e9bdd9087d414735b. MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025
  Corey Haines; the repository's LICENSE is copied as copy-editing/LICENSE.
  Unmodified.
- find-skills: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills, path skills/find-skills
  (SKILL.md), read at commit a80e4c9d12d607631249d4d7d059f835d4b2f13a. MIT
  License, Copyright (c) 2026 Vercel, Inc.; the repository's LICENSE is copied
  as find-skills/LICENSE. Modified: appended a section for IeumOffice
  ("In IeumOffice") at the end of SKILL.md.

Hangul (HWP) document format

The HWP/HWPX editor is built on rhwp (https://github.com/edwardkim/rhwp,
MIT License). As required by Hancom Inc. for software developed with its
published HWP format document:

본 제품은 한글과컴퓨터의 한글 문서 파일(.hwp) 공개 문서를 참고하여
개발하였습니다.

(This product was developed with reference to Hancom's published document on
the Hangul document file format (.hwp).)

==========================

Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see http://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see http://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see http://www.opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-
                    from                                compatible? (1)

    0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes
    1.3 thru 1.5.2  1.2         1995-1999   CNRI        yes
    1.6             1.5.2       2000        CNRI        no
    2.0             1.6         2000        BeOpen.com  no
    1.6.1           1.6         2001        CNRI        yes (2)
    2.1             2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         no
    2.0.1           2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.1           2.1+2.0.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.2           2.1.1       2002        PSF         yes
    2.1.3           2.1.2       2002        PSF         yes
    2.2 and above   2.1.1       2001-now    PSF         yes

Footnotes:

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under
    the GPL.  All Python licenses, unlike the GPL, let you distribute
    a modified version without making your changes open source.  The
    GPL-compatible licenses make it possible to combine Python with
    other software that is released under the GPL; the others don't.

(2) According to Richard Stallman, 1.6.1 is not GPL-compatible,
    because its license has a choice of law clause.  According to
    CNRI, however, Stallman's lawyer has told CNRI's lawyer that 1.6.1
    is "not incompatible" with the GPL.

Thanks to the many outside volunteers who have worked under Guido's
direction to make these releases possible.

7. draw.io (diagram editor)
========================================================================

draw.io v32.6.9 (https://github.com/jgraph/drawio), Apache License 2.0.
Copyright (c) 2006-2026, JGraph Holdings Ltd
Copyright (c) 2006-2026, draw.io AG

The diagram editor ships the files of the draw.io release asset
https://github.com/jgraph/drawio/releases/download/v32.6.9/draw.war
(SHA-256 31afc82b7920c409d0591f6126ccb6c377d7800e7f11ab324f88bdf1e4249ce7) under resources/modules/diagram/drawio.
The editor itself (mxGraph core, the application scripts, its own converters for Gliffy, binary Visio, Mermaid and org charts, styles, resources, UI images and plugins). js/app.min.js and js/viewer-static.min.js contain a Base64 encoder/decoder adapted from http://www.webtoolkit.info/, which the file header credits.

Changes from the release:

- 235 release files are left out: server parts, development sources,
  bundles and helpers the editor does not load, cloud connection pages,
  service workers, and parts under licenses this application does not ship
  (PlantUML, ELK, libavoid, and the Glyphicons sharing icons, CC BY 3.0),
  matched by these patterns:
    WEB-INF/**
    META-INF/**
    js/diagramly/**
    js/grapheditor/**
    js/plantuml/**
    js/libavoid-js/**
    js/elk/**
    js/integrate.min.js
    js/viewer.min.js
    connect/**
    teams.html
    onedrive3.html
    js/onedrive/**
    service-worker*
    workbox-*
    js/deflate/base64.js
    images/glyphicons_*.png
- js/extensions.min.js is the release file (4632095 bytes) with the bytes
  of the following files of the same release removed, each found verbatim
  exactly once inside it (byte offsets in the release file). Nothing else in
  it is changed; the result is 3084176 bytes, SHA-256 276ff2a892efc41b9921326d8e6a5c7bb0aaf4b98353eac7b6ad21adfb651a30.
    js/elk/drawio-elk.min.js: bytes 1380052-2303385
    js/libavoid-js/libavoid.min.js: bytes 3960573-4532761
    js/libavoid-js/libavoid-routing.js: bytes 4532762-4585157
  Those files are ELK (EPL-2.0) and libavoid with its routing core
  (LGPL-2.1), which this application does not ship.
- Every other shipped file is byte-identical to the release. When the
  editor page is served, the application adds its own bridge script to
  index.html in memory; the shipped file itself is not changed.
